notice: SYNTHETIC EVALUATION SCAFFOLDING. Every passage below was written for this repository to exercise retrieval mechanics. It is not licensed medical content, it has not been reviewed by a clinician, and it must never be presented, quoted or relied on as medical information. Its only purpose is to make Recall@K, MRR and nDCG computable over text whose correct answers are known by construction. Replace it with a licensed, de-identified, clinician-reviewed corpus before any retrieval number is treated as evidence about real performance.

chunks.label: c-hla-1
chunks.text: HLA-B27 is a class I major histocompatibility antigen that shows a strong association with ankylosing spondylitis. The association is far from universal: many carriers of HLA-B27 never develop inflammatory back pain, and the antigen is present in a minority of the general population, so it is used to support a clinical diagnosis rather than to establish one on its own.

chunks.label: c-hla-2
chunks.text: Testing for HLA-B27 is most informative when the pre-test probability of axial spondyloarthritis is intermediate. In a patient with inflammatory back pain, sacroiliitis on imaging and a positive HLA-B27 result, the combination supports the diagnosis; a negative result in the same patient does not exclude it.

chunks.label: c-cyp3a4-1
chunks.text: CYP3A4 is the most abundant cytochrome P450 isoenzyme in the human liver and intestine and takes part in the metabolism of a large share of prescribed medicines. Strong inhibitors of CYP3A4 reduce the clearance of substrate drugs and raise their plasma concentrations, while strong inducers do the opposite.

chunks.label: c-cyp3a4-2
chunks.text: When a CYP3A4 inhibitor is started in a patient already taking a narrow therapeutic index substrate, the dose of the substrate may need to be reduced and the response monitored. Grapefruit juice inhibits intestinal CYP3A4 and can raise the bioavailability of some oral substrates.

chunks.label: c-brca1
chunks.text: BRCA1 is a tumour suppressor gene involved in homologous recombination repair of double-strand DNA breaks. Pathogenic variants in BRCA1 are inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern and are associated with a substantially increased lifetime risk of breast and ovarian cancer.

chunks.label: c-brca2
chunks.text: BRCA2 also participates in homologous recombination repair. Pathogenic variants confer an increased risk of breast cancer in both sexes and of ovarian, pancreatic and prostate cancer, with a risk profile that differs from BRCA1 in the pattern and typical age of onset.

chunks.label: c-il6
chunks.text: IL-6 is a pleiotropic cytokine released by macrophages, fibroblasts and endothelial cells during inflammation. It drives the hepatic acute phase response, including the production of C-reactive protein, and contributes to fever and to the anaemia seen in chronic inflammatory disease.

chunks.label: c-her2
chunks.text: HER2 is a receptor tyrosine kinase encoded by the ERBB2 gene. Amplification or overexpression of HER2 defines a distinct subgroup of breast tumours with a characteristic natural history, and receptor status is reported alongside oestrogen and progesterone receptor results.

chunks.label: c-hba1c
chunks.text: HbA1c reflects average glycaemia over the preceding two to three months because glucose binds irreversibly to haemoglobin over the life span of the red cell. A value of 6.5% or above on two occasions is conventionally used as a diagnostic threshold, and conditions that shorten red cell survival make the result unreliable.

chunks.label: c-digoxin
chunks.text: Digoxin inhibits the Na+/K+-ATPase pump in the cardiac myocyte membrane. The resulting rise in intracellular sodium reduces calcium extrusion through the sodium-calcium exchanger, raising intracellular calcium and increasing contractile force. Hypokalaemia increases binding to the pump and therefore the risk of toxicity.

chunks.label: c-warfarin
chunks.text: Warfarin inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase and so reduces the synthesis of clotting factors II, VII, IX and X. Its effect is monitored with the international normalised ratio, and because factor VII has the shortest half-life the INR rises before full antithrombotic effect is established.

chunks.label: c-amoxicillin
chunks.text: Amoxicillin is an aminopenicillin with improved oral absorption compared with ampicillin. It acts by binding penicillin-binding proteins and disrupting cell wall cross-linking, and it is inactivated by beta-lactamase unless combined with an inhibitor such as clavulanic acid.

chunks.label: c-mi
chunks.text: Myocardial infarction is myocardial cell death caused by prolonged ischaemia. It is distinguished from unstable angina by the release of cardiac troponin above the reference limit, and the electrocardiogram separates presentations with persistent ST elevation from those without.

chunks.label: c-hypertension
chunks.text: Hypertension is a sustained elevation of arterial blood pressure and is usually asymptomatic until end-organ damage appears. It is a leading modifiable contributor to stroke, ischaemic heart disease, heart failure and chronic kidney disease, and diagnosis rests on repeated measurement rather than a single reading.

chunks.label: c-hf
chunks.text: Heart failure is a clinical syndrome in which cardiac output is inadequate for the metabolic demands of the tissues, or is adequate only at the cost of raised filling pressures. Breathlessness on exertion, orthopnoea, fatigue and peripheral oedema are the characteristic features, and neurohormonal activation drives progression.

chunks.label: c-erdheim
chunks.text: Erdheim-Chester disease is a rare non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis characterised by infiltration of tissues with foamy histiocytes. Symmetrical sclerosis of the long bone metadiaphyses is the classic radiological finding, and the disease may also involve the retroperitoneum, the central nervous system and the heart.

chunks.label: c-dm1
chunks.text: Type 1 diabetes mellitus results from immune-mediated destruction of pancreatic beta cells, producing absolute insulin deficiency. Presentation is often abrupt, with weight loss, marked polyuria and a tendency to ketoacidosis, and treatment requires insulin replacement from diagnosis.

chunks.label: c-dm2
chunks.text: Type 2 diabetes mellitus arises from a combination of insulin resistance and progressive beta cell failure. Onset is usually gradual and may be detected on screening before symptoms appear, and management begins with lifestyle measures alongside oral glucose-lowering therapy.

chunks.label: c-cross-1
chunks.text: Acute kidney injury is staged by the rise in serum creatinine from the patient's baseline and by urine output over a defined period. Stage 1 corresponds to the smallest sustained rise, and each subsequent stage reflects a larger increment or a longer period of reduced urine output.

chunks.label: c-cross-2
chunks.text: The continuation of the staging discussion notes that creatinine is a delayed marker: the concentration lags behind the fall in glomerular filtration rate, so a patient may already have significant injury when the first abnormal result is reported. Urine output criteria therefore detect some cases earlier.

chunks.label: c-table-dose
chunks.caption: Table 7.2 Illustrative oral dosing intervals for the synthetic evaluation corpus
chunks.text: Table 7.2 Illustrative oral dosing intervals. Drug | Illustrative adult oral dose | Interval. Amoxicillin | 500 mg | every 8 hours. Metformin | 500 mg | twice daily with food. Atorvastatin | 20 mg | once daily. Ramipril | 2.5 mg | once daily. These figures are synthetic and exist only to give the evaluation corpus a table to retrieve.

chunks.label: c-formula-crcl
chunks.caption: Estimated creatinine clearance
chunks.text: Estimated creatinine clearance = ((140 - age) x weight in kg) / (72 x serum creatinine in mg/dL), multiplied by 0.85 for female patients. The estimate assumes stable renal function and becomes unreliable when creatinine is changing rapidly or when body composition is unusual.

chunks.label: c-formula-map
chunks.caption: Mean arterial pressure
chunks.text: Mean arterial pressure = diastolic pressure + (systolic pressure - diastolic pressure) / 3. The approximation assumes a normal heart rate; at high rates diastole shortens and the true mean lies closer to the arithmetic average of the two pressures.

chunks.label: c-figure-cardiac
chunks.caption: Figure 9.1 Pressure and volume changes through one cardiac cycle
chunks.text: Figure 9.1 Pressure and volume changes through one cardiac cycle. The figure plots left ventricular, aortic and left atrial pressure against time, with the ventricular volume trace beneath. Isovolumetric contraction, ejection, isovolumetric relaxation and filling are labelled, and valve opening and closure are marked on the pressure curves.

chunks.label: c-figure-nephron
chunks.caption: Figure 9.2 Sites of action of diuretic classes along the nephron
chunks.text: Figure 9.2 Sites of action of diuretic classes along the nephron. The schematic follows the tubule from the proximal convoluted tubule through the loop of Henle to the collecting duct, marking where carbonic anhydrase inhibitors, loop diuretics, thiazides and potassium-sparing agents act.

chunks.label: c-bp-guideline
chunks.text: This synthetic guideline states an office blood pressure target below 130/80 mmHg for most treated adults, provided the target is reached without symptomatic hypotension. It notes that the target should be individualised in frailty and in older patients, and that home readings run lower than office readings.

chunks.label: c-bp-course
chunks.text: These synthetic revision notes state an office blood pressure target below 140/90 mmHg for treated adults. The figure conflicts with the synthetic guideline in the same corpus, and the pair exists so that retrieval of a disagreement between sources of different authority can be observed.

chunks.label: c-guide-af
chunks.text: In this synthetic guideline, the decision to anticoagulate in atrial fibrillation is based on estimated stroke risk rather than on the pattern of the arrhythmia, and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation is treated as carrying the same risk as persistent atrial fibrillation for that purpose.

chunks.label: c-guide-sepsis
chunks.text: This synthetic guideline recommends that blood cultures be taken before antimicrobial therapy where doing so does not materially delay treatment, and that the initial regimen be reviewed once culture results are available so that therapy can be narrowed.

chunks.label: c-course-abg
chunks.text: A stepwise reading of an arterial blood gas begins with the pH, then the carbon dioxide tension, then the bicarbonate, and finally asks whether compensation is appropriate for the duration of the disturbance. A mixed picture is suggested when compensation is greater or smaller than expected.

chunks.label: c-course-list
chunks.text: Causes of a raised anion gap metabolic acidosis in these synthetic notes: lactic acidosis; ketoacidosis; established renal failure; and ingestion of certain toxic alcohols. Each entry is a heading in the notes rather than a full account of the underlying mechanism.

chunks.label: c-q-hla
chunks.text: Question 14. A 24-year-old presents with several months of inflammatory back pain and morning stiffness lasting more than an hour. Which antigen is most strongly associated with the suspected diagnosis? A. HLA-DR4  B. HLA-B27  C. HLA-DQ2  D. HLA-A3

chunks.label: c-q-digoxin
chunks.text: Question 22. Which membrane transporter is directly inhibited by digoxin in the cardiac myocyte? A. The sodium-calcium exchanger  B. The Na+/K+-ATPase pump  C. The L-type calcium channel  D. The sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase

chunks.label: c-q-explanation
chunks.text: Explanation for question 22. Inhibition of the sodium pump raises intracellular sodium, which reduces the driving force for calcium extrusion by the sodium-calcium exchanger. The exchanger is affected indirectly, which is why it is not the transporter the question asks about.

chunks.label: c-key-1
chunks.text: Answer key, synthetic evaluation set, questions 11 to 25. 11 C. 12 A. 13 D. 14 B. 15 A. 16 C. 17 B. 18 D. 19 A. 20 C. 21 B. 22 B. 23 D. 24 A. 25 C. The key records the recorded letter only and carries no reasoning.

chunks.label: c-ref-troponin
chunks.text: Cardiac troponin I and T are structural proteins of the contractile apparatus and are released when myocytes are damaged. A rising or falling pattern on serial sampling distinguishes acute injury from a chronically raised concentration, which is common in renal impairment and in structural heart disease.

chunks.label: c-ref-asthma
chunks.text: Asthma is characterised by variable airflow limitation and airway hyper-responsiveness with an underlying inflammatory process. Variability over time and in response to bronchodilator is what distinguishes it from fixed obstruction, and objective demonstration of that variability supports the diagnosis.

chunks.label: c-ref-copd
chunks.text: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is characterised by persistent airflow limitation that is not fully reversible. Spirometry after bronchodilator is required for the diagnosis, and the clinical picture combines emphysematous destruction with chronic airway inflammation in proportions that vary between patients.

chunks.label: c-ref-anaemia
chunks.text: Anaemia is classified by red cell size into microcytic, normocytic and macrocytic groups, and this classification narrows the differential before further tests are ordered. Iron studies, reticulocyte count and a blood film usually separate the common causes within each group.

chunks.label: c-ref-thyroid
chunks.text: Primary hypothyroidism produces a raised thyroid stimulating hormone with a low free thyroxine, because the pituitary responds to the falling peripheral hormone. In secondary disease the stimulating hormone is inappropriately normal or low despite the low thyroxine.

chunks.label: c-ref-stroke
chunks.text: An ischaemic stroke follows occlusion of a cerebral artery, while a haemorrhagic stroke follows rupture. The two cannot be separated clinically with sufficient confidence, so imaging is required before any treatment that would be harmful in the presence of bleeding.

chunks.label: c-ref-hepatitis
chunks.text: Acute hepatitis produces a predominantly hepatocellular pattern of liver enzyme rise, with aminotransferases raised out of proportion to alkaline phosphatase. A cholestatic pattern shows the reverse, and the distinction directs the initial investigation towards parenchymal or biliary disease.

chunks.label: c-ref-electrolyte
chunks.text: Hyponatraemia is assessed by first establishing the serum osmolality, then the volume status, and then the urinary sodium concentration. The sequence matters because the same sodium concentration arises from mechanisms whose treatments are opposite to one another.

chunks.label: c-ref-immunisation
chunks.text: Herd protection describes the indirect protection of unvaccinated individuals that arises when a sufficient proportion of a population is immune. The threshold proportion depends on how transmissible the organism is, so a highly transmissible infection requires a higher coverage.

chunks.label: c-ref-statistics
chunks.text: Sensitivity is the proportion of those with the condition whom a test identifies, and specificity the proportion without it whom the test correctly clears. Predictive values depend additionally on how common the condition is in the population being tested.

chunks.label: c-ref-ethics
chunks.text: Valid consent requires that the person has capacity for the decision in question, has been given the information a reasonable person would want, and is deciding voluntarily. Capacity is assessed for a specific decision at a specific time rather than as a general attribute.

chunks.label: c-ref-abx-resistance
chunks.text: Beta-lactamase production is a common mechanism of resistance to penicillins, and the enzyme hydrolyses the beta-lactam ring before the drug can bind its target. Combining the antibiotic with a beta-lactamase inhibitor restores activity against organisms whose resistance depends on that enzyme.

chunks.label: c-d-hla-dr4
chunks.text: HLA-DR4 is a class II major histocompatibility antigen associated with rheumatoid arthritis in several populations. The strength of the association varies with the specific allele and with ancestry, and the antigen is not used as a diagnostic test in routine rheumatology practice.

chunks.label: c-d-hla-dq2
chunks.text: HLA-DQ2 and HLA-DQ8 are class II antigens present in almost everyone with coeliac disease. Because they are also common in unaffected people their value is in exclusion: a negative result makes the diagnosis very unlikely, while a positive result adds little on its own.

chunks.label: c-d-mhc
chunks.text: The major histocompatibility complex encodes class I antigens expressed on nearly all nucleated cells and class II antigens restricted largely to professional antigen presenting cells. Class I molecules present peptides to cytotoxic T cells and class II molecules to helper T cells.

chunks.label: c-d-cyp2d6
chunks.text: CYP2D6 shows marked genetic polymorphism, and the population divides into poor, intermediate, extensive and ultrarapid metabolisers. For a prodrug activated by CYP2D6 a poor metaboliser may obtain little effect, while an ultrarapid metaboliser may reach unexpectedly high active concentrations.

chunks.label: c-d-cyp2c19
chunks.text: CYP2C19 activity varies with genotype and influences the metabolism of several proton pump inhibitors and of clopidogrel, which requires the enzyme for activation. Loss-of-function variants are more frequent in some populations than others.

chunks.label: c-d-cyp1a2
chunks.text: CYP1A2 is induced by polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in tobacco smoke, so clearance of its substrates falls when a patient stops smoking. The change is a property of the smoke rather than of nicotine, and nicotine replacement does not maintain the induction.

chunks.label: c-d-pgp
chunks.text: P-glycoprotein is an efflux transporter in the intestinal epithelium, the biliary canaliculus and the blood-brain barrier. Inhibition raises the systemic exposure of substrate drugs, and several inhibitors of CYP3A4 inhibit P-glycoprotein as well, so the two effects often occur together.

chunks.label: c-d-heparin
chunks.text: Unfractionated heparin potentiates antithrombin and is monitored with the activated partial thromboplastin time, while low molecular weight heparin has a more predictable response and is usually given by weight without routine monitoring. Neither agent depends on vitamin K.

chunks.label: c-d-doac
chunks.text: Direct oral anticoagulants inhibit thrombin or activated factor X directly and do not require routine monitoring of the international normalised ratio. Dose adjustment depends chiefly on renal function, age and weight rather than on a coagulation result.

chunks.label: c-d-inr
chunks.text: The international normalised ratio standardises the prothrombin time against an international reference preparation so that results are comparable between laboratories. It is also raised in liver disease and in vitamin K deficiency, where it reflects synthetic function rather than anticoagulation.

chunks.label: c-d-cephalosporin
chunks.text: Cephalosporins are beta-lactam agents grouped into generations that broadly describe their spectrum. Later generations gain activity against Gram-negative organisms while often losing some activity against staphylococci, and stability to beta-lactamase varies within each generation.

chunks.label: c-d-flucloxacillin
chunks.text: Flucloxacillin is a penicillinase-stable penicillin whose side chain protects the beta-lactam ring from staphylococcal beta-lactamase. Its spectrum is narrow, and it has little useful activity against Gram-negative organisms or enterococci.

chunks.label: c-d-macrolide
chunks.text: Macrolides bind the 50S ribosomal subunit and inhibit protein synthesis. Several are inhibitors of CYP3A4, so starting one in a patient taking a substrate can raise that drug concentration, and the interaction is a common reason to choose an alternative agent.

chunks.label: c-d-fructosamine
chunks.text: Fructosamine reflects glycation of serum proteins over the preceding two to three weeks and is used when haemoglobin-based measurement is unreliable, for instance in haemoglobinopathy or after a recent transfusion. Its reference intervals are laboratory specific.

chunks.label: c-d-cgm
chunks.text: Continuous glucose monitoring reports interstitial glucose at short intervals and describes time in range, time above range and glycaemic variability. It complements a longer-term average measure rather than replacing it, because the two summarise different windows.

chunks.label: c-d-fasting-glucose
chunks.text: A fasting plasma glucose of 7.0 mmol/L or above on two occasions is a conventional diagnostic threshold, and an oral glucose tolerance test remains useful where fasting values are equivocal. Thresholds differ between the fasting and post-load measurements.

chunks.label: c-d-betablocker
chunks.text: Beta blockers reduce heart rate and contractility by antagonising beta-adrenoceptors, lowering myocardial oxygen demand. In heart failure with reduced ejection fraction they are introduced at low dose and increased slowly, because the initial negative inotropic effect can be poorly tolerated.

chunks.label: c-d-ccb
chunks.text: Dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers act mainly on vascular smooth muscle and lower peripheral resistance, while the non-dihydropyridine agents also slow conduction through the atrioventricular node. The distinction matters when rate control rather than vasodilatation is intended.

chunks.label: c-d-sodium-channel
chunks.text: Fast sodium channels open at the start of the cardiac action potential and produce rapid depolarisation in atrial and ventricular myocytes. Agents that block them slow conduction, and their effect is greater at faster rates because more channels are in the inactivated state.

chunks.label: c-d-serca
chunks.text: The sarcoplasmic reticulum calcium ATPase returns calcium to intracellular stores during relaxation, and its activity is regulated by phospholamban. Impaired function prolongs relaxation and contributes to diastolic dysfunction independently of contractile strength.

chunks.label: c-d-cardiomyopathy
chunks.text: Dilated cardiomyopathy describes ventricular dilatation with impaired systolic function in the absence of loading conditions or coronary disease sufficient to explain it. Causes include genetic variants, previous myocarditis, toxins and sustained tachycardia.

chunks.label: c-d-valve
chunks.text: Aortic stenosis produces a pressure-loaded left ventricle that hypertrophies to maintain wall stress. Symptoms appear late and their onset marks a change in prognosis, because the hypertrophied ventricle eventually fails to compensate for the fixed obstruction.

chunks.label: c-d-preload
chunks.text: Stroke volume depends on preload, afterload and contractility. Increasing end-diastolic fibre length raises the force of contraction up to a point, beyond which further filling does not increase output and instead raises filling pressures.

chunks.label: c-d-lch
chunks.text: Langerhans cell histiocytosis is a clonal proliferation of cells with dendritic features, and its presentation ranges from a solitary bone lesion to multisystem disease. It is distinguished from non-Langerhans histiocytoses by immunophenotype rather than by site.

chunks.label: c-d-sarcoid
chunks.text: Sarcoidosis is a multisystem granulomatous disorder of unknown cause, most often affecting the lungs and intrathoracic lymph nodes. Non-caseating granulomas are the histological hallmark, and the differential includes infection and other granulomatous conditions.

chunks.label: c-d-formula-bmi
chunks.caption: Body mass index
chunks.text: Body mass index = weight in kilograms / (height in metres squared). The index does not distinguish lean from fat mass, so it misclassifies people with unusual body composition in either direction, and interpretation thresholds differ between populations.

chunks.label: c-d-formula-anion
chunks.caption: Anion gap
chunks.text: Anion gap = (sodium + potassium) - (chloride + bicarbonate), or sodium - (chloride + bicarbonate) when potassium is omitted. The value must be interpreted alongside the albumin concentration, because albumin contributes most of the unmeasured anion.

chunks.label: c-d-figure-ecg
chunks.caption: Figure 9.3 Timing of the electrocardiogram against the cardiac action potential
chunks.text: Figure 9.3 Timing of the electrocardiogram against the cardiac action potential. The schematic aligns the P wave, QRS complex and T wave with atrial and ventricular depolarisation and repolarisation, and marks where the refractory periods fall relative to the surface trace.

chunks.label: c-d-figure-spirometry
chunks.caption: Figure 9.4 Flow-volume loops in obstructive and restrictive disease
chunks.text: Figure 9.4 Flow-volume loops in obstructive and restrictive disease. The figure contrasts the scooped expiratory limb of airflow obstruction with the narrow, tall loop of a restrictive defect, and marks where a fixed large-airway obstruction flattens both limbs.

chunks.label: c-d-q-cyp
chunks.text: Question 18. A patient stabilised on a narrow therapeutic index drug is started on a macrolide antibiotic and becomes toxic. Which enzyme is most likely responsible? A. CYP1A2  B. CYP2D6  C. CYP3A4  D. CYP2C19

chunks.label: c-d-q-hba1c
chunks.text: Question 25. Which measurement best reflects average glycaemia over the preceding two to three months? A. Fasting plasma glucose  B. Random plasma glucose  C. HbA1c  D. Fructosamine

chunks.label: c-d-q-explanation-2
chunks.text: Explanation for question 25. The correct option reflects a window set by the life span of the red cell. Fructosamine covers a shorter window, and a single plasma glucose describes only the moment of sampling, which is why neither is the best answer here.

chunks.label: c-d-bp-elderly
chunks.text: This synthetic guideline adds that in adults over eighty, or in those with significant frailty, the treated target should be relaxed and the decision reviewed against symptoms, postural change and overall burden of treatment rather than applied uniformly.

chunks.label: c-d-bp-home
chunks.text: Home and ambulatory readings run lower than readings taken in a clinic, and this synthetic guideline states that a target expressed for office measurement should be reduced correspondingly when out-of-office readings are used for monitoring.
